text:
𝗔𝘁 𝟵 𝗣𝗠 𝗼𝗻 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝟭𝟳, 𝟮𝟬𝟬𝟬, 𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗶𝘁 𝗮 𝗣𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗽𝘀 𝘀𝗲𝗺𝗶𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝗻 𝗔𝗹𝗯𝘂𝗾𝘂𝗲𝗿𝗾𝘂𝗲, 𝗡𝗲𝘄 𝗠𝗲𝘅𝗶𝗰𝗼. 
The fire was put out in 10 minutes but smoke and water destroyed millions of chips. The plant was the sole source for two customers: 𝗡𝗼𝗸𝗶𝗮 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗘𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘀𝘀𝗼𝗻.

Within days, 𝗡𝗼𝗸𝗶𝗮 𝗺𝗼𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝗰𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗺𝘀. They locked up spare capacity at every other Philips plant on Earth, redesigned circuit boards to accept alternate chips, and found new suppliers in Japan and the US.

𝗘𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘀𝘀𝗼𝗻? It accepted Philips' first reassuring estimate. By the time it realized the truth, every available chip in the world was already booked by Nokia.

The result: Ericsson lost $400M, ceded 3% market share, and within 9 months exited the phone business. Nokia's market share hit 30%.

Both had the same data. Only one acted. Which one are you?

Stay tuned for daily one such Stories.
